title: Component Design Best Practices knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Component Design Best Practices”?
options: Component Design Best Practices means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Component Design Best Practices removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Component Design Best Practices should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Component Design Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Component Design Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Component Design Best Practices is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Keeping components focused” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Keeping components focused” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Keeping components focused” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Keeping components focused” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Keeping components focused” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Keeping components focused” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Keeping components focused” under Component Design Best Practices. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Component Design Best Practices”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
